Flesh Made Fear — Classic Horror Reborn

Flesh Made Fear takes everything we loved about PSX-era survival horror and cranks it to eleven. It’s a grim, atmospheric descent into bio-occult madness where every bullet, save token, and step matters.

From Tainted Pact Games (Suffer the Night, Massacre at the Mirage), this one nails the balance between nostalgia and innovation — fixed and dynamic cameras, limited saves, and puzzle-driven storytelling all wrapped in modern cinematics and sound design that drip tension.

Two playable characters, scarce ammo, and grotesque enemy designs make survival feel earned. It’s brutal, methodical, and unapologetically old-school — exactly what the genre needed.

Verdict: If you miss Resident Evil 1-3 or Silent Hill but want something fresh, Flesh Made Fear delivers fear with teeth.

[h1]Welcome To Rotwood[/h1]

I enjoy Survival Horror games and this definitely scratches that itch. Itchy. Tasty.

[b][u]PROS:[/u][/b]

➕ [b]Classic Survival Horror Formula;[/b] It's the classic ingredients for a Survival Horror: tank controls, fixed camera angles, inventory management, puzzle solving, slow-moving zombies, and deciding between fight or flight.

➕ [b]Story;[/b] The premise is interesting enough, and they've thought about it from several angles.

➕ [b]Environmental Storytelling;[/b] The notes/audio tapes complement the environmental storytelling excellently. Together, they paint a coherent picture of what happened in your surroundings. It makes me feel like my character is actually walking through locations where things happened, rather than just theater props. It also makes me more invested in interpreting environmental clues.

➕ [b]Voice acting;[/b] Much of the game is voice-acted, as are many of the notes (= audio tapes). I recognize certain names too like LaynaLazar, which is a welcome surprise.

➕ [b]Movement & Menus;[/b] Overall, moving my character and navigating menus feels OK. I particularly like that Quick Turn is bound to Q so that I can press it exactly when I intend to.

[b][u]NEUTRAL/NOTES:[/u][/b]

⚪ [b]Conserve Ammo;[/b] This is just a note, but conserving ammo is very much a part of this game. If you find opportunities to save bullets, you better take them.

⚪ [b]Reloading;[/b] Interestingly, there doesn't seem to be a button for reloading the gun. It has to be initiated from inventory screen by "using" bullets.

⚪ [b]Length;[/b] A minor note from me, but I feel like this game could've gone on a little longer. Then again, it didn't overstay its welcome either.

⚪ [b]Machine Gun;[/b] I somehow managed to go through the entire game without finding the machine gun? Despite the fact that I had unlocked the room it was in and searched it.

[b][u]CONS:[/u][/b]

➖ [b]Aiming;[/b] Aiming at an enemy feels clunky. It doesn't auto-aim at the nearest enemy when I press aim; I have to Quick Turn, point at the enemy and hope it aimed correctly. It does lock onto the target, but I have to move the laser sight until it does, which never seems to move as I intend. When it lock onto a target, I'm often confused about why it doesn't move anymore, especially when the shot looks like it would miss.

➖ [b]Specific Camera Angles;[/b] I almost got lost at one point because the camera angle hid one of the doorways. I only had a vague memory of it because I had played the demo before.

➖ [b]Weapon Unequipped;[/b] The game has an annoying habit of unequipping my weapon when I move between zones.

Flesh Made Fear is one of the most gorgeous games I’ve played this year. Yeah, we all know it’s inspired by Resident Evil — but let’s be honest, this isn’t some cheap knockoff. It borrows the concept, sure, but it builds something unique out of it.

One thing I really love is how much the game focuses on story and lore. Every journal or note you find isn’t just some wall of text — you can actually listen to them, fully voiced, and the voice actors did a solid job too. It’s a small touch, but it makes exploring way more immersive.

I’ve played for about one or two hours so far, and another thing that stood out to me is how logical the exploration feels. For example, if there’s a locked box in a room, the clue or note related to the code is usually nearby — no need to run across the entire map just to find one tiny pin number. Don’t get me wrong, I love games that make you search every corner, but this one has a more relaxed, chill pace. You can take your time, experiment a bit, explore, and then boom — you find your answer.

It’s got atmosphere, mystery, and enough charm to stand on its own. Definitely worth checking out if you’re into story-driven horror with Resident Evil vibes but a more laid-back flow.

[i]Honestly, this feels like digging up an old PS1 disc and realizing it still runs and still scares the crap out of you.[/i]

The [b]fixed cameras[/b], [b]grainy textures[/b], and [b]clunky movement[/b] somehow [i]work perfectly together[/i]. It’s that old school horror vibe where nothing jumps at you the fear just [i]sits there[/i], heavy, waiting.

Yeah, it’s rough around the edges, but that’s the charm. You’re not supposed to feel in control and that constant unease? That’s exactly what makes it great.

It’s not trying to be [i]Resident Evil 4 Remake[/i]. It’s trying to remind you what it felt like when survival horror actually meant [i]surviving[/i].

If you miss that weird mix of [b]fear and nostalgia[/b], when sweaty palms and cursed camera angles were half the fun… this is [i]it[/i].

[quote]Feels like 1999 again in the best (and most cursed) way possible.[/quote]

Flesh Made Fear makes an effort to recapture the look and feel of classic survival horror games such as the original Resident Evil trilogy. The voice acting in the game contains moments similar to the classic lines "I hope this isn't Chris' blood" and "You were almost a Jill sandwich." That's not to say the voice acting is bad, it's a very deliberate choice to recreate part of what we love about those games and it does it very well.

The gameplay does exactly what it sets out to do in classic survival horror fashion with tank controls, stop and aim shooting, and the fixed camera. Resources are limited in the game, though by the time you reach the end of an area you'll find you have just enough health items and ammo to make it through. Some fights in the game do offer some frustration and tension, but they work well to fuel the fear you should have playing a game of this nature. Puzzles thankfully aren't too difficult or frustrating and although there was a moment or two of not understanding how to progress it never seemed like it was the game's fault moreso a lack of exploring every avenue available.

The game offers the simple plot of a mad scientist whose creations are set loose in a town and a group of special ops style people arriving there to capture him and find their lost comrade. Audio logs found throughout the game tell of the game's mad scientist looking to find a way to control the human mind and of other townsfolk's plights.

This game is both a love letter to those survival horror games of yore and something that maintains its own identity. Overall this is an excellent addition to the survival horror genre and a game I'll be happy to replay every now and again.

Flesh Made Fear is a shameless love letter to Resident Evil’s PS1-era roots with tank controls, awkward camera angles, questionable voice acting, and all. It wears its influences proudly, and in doing so, manages to capture the same mix of charm and frustration that defined the genre in the late ‘90s.

The visual aesthetic is fantastic with gritty pixel art, grotesque gore, and character models that look straight out of a forgotten survival horror gem. Everything from the item management to the deliberate pacing and sound design feels deliberately “old-school,” and it works surprisingly well if you’re after that nostalgic fix.

That said, the aiming system is easily the weakest link for me. It feels clunky and lacks any sort of auto-aim assistance, forcing you to manually shuffle and line up shots in a way that feels more frustrating than tense. Enemy placement can also feel a bit cheap at times, you’ll occasionally get ambushed and stun-locked without much chance to recover.

Still, for all its flaws, Flesh Made Fear delivers a genuine throwback experience that few modern entries manage to pull off. If you grew up with Resident Evil and Silent Hill and miss that era’s peculiar blend of horror and jank, this is absolutely worth your time.

I've been a huge fan of Tained Pact since the demo for [i]Suffer the Night[/i], and each one just feels like it's getting better and better. I dare say this is their masterpiece. It plays well, it sounds great, the voice acting is awesome, and the vibes are immaculate.

Almost. 

1. The bosses feel a little like bullet-sponges, and you spend more time running around in circles that attacking them.
2. The dodge mechanic is alright, except you seem to only dodge in the direction your facing...or I haven't figured out how to back-step with it yet...And it doesn't get you OUT of being surrounded. At that point yer screwed.
3. The lighting indoors is a bit TOO dark, even for a game like this. I don't mind low/atmospheric lighting, but pure black is a little annoying, especially when the areas are so well put together and works of art in their own right.

Aside from those (incredibly) minor snags, I think this game is totally worth picking up for anyone who remotely enjoys survival horror games. Get it. You won't regret it.

EDIT: I finally beat the game (on Normal) and hilariously, the final boss was actually a lot of fun and I didn't find it to be too much of a punishing encounter. The game is awesome, and I honestly love anything Tainted Pact puts out. It's totally worth your time at full price, and especially if you're a fan of survival horror games. Can't wait for a sequel (if there is going to be one lol HINT HINT)

Flesh Made Fear is a retro-style survival horror game that leans hard into everything we loved about 90s horror: fixed angles, chunky environments, dramatic villains, and that delicious mix of camp and dread. You’re jumping between two characters, piecing together what went horribly wrong in a very cursed little town crawling with awful things and worse secrets.

Pros
✔ The voice acting is fantastic – Especially the Ripper. Every time he spoke I was like, “Yep, that’s exactly the kind of maniacal evil we signed up for.”
✔ Runs beautifully – Seriously, it’s smooth as butter. Not even a hiccup on my end and so well optimized.
✔ Peak retro horror energy – This is exactly how modern throwback horror should be done. It feels nostalgic with the improvements we have grown accustom to in modern gaming.

Cons
❌ Camp = predictable moments – Sometimes you can see where a story beat is going just because it’s leaning into that old-school style so hard which is the trade off for the nostalgia factor.
❌ Replay layout is a bit odd – The way both characters share and repeat certain areas, but then have unique parts in others made my second run feel a little patchwork.
❌ Did not enjoy the map – It exists. That’s about as much praise as I can give it.

Conclusion
I had an absolute blast with this one. It gave me all the nods to classic horror I was hoping for, and honestly, Tainted Pact outdid themselves. You can feel the passion in every room, every detail, every ridiculous villain moment — and it’s wild seeing such a small team make something that could go toe-to-toe with big studio horror titles. I’m not shocked people online are loving it; I’m just happy I get to be one of them.

Flesh Made Fear is an unabashed homage to both the Resident Evil series and general 80's cheesy horror movies and I'm all for it. The game's a fun ride combining elements of primarily Resident Evil 1 (a team of SWAT-like special agents being dispatched to a small country town in the woods and being able to pick a male or female playable character) and 3 (much more action-focused and linear gameplay flow with a dodge mechanic and ammo crafting).

I've only beaten Natalya's run and I'm taking a break before doing a hardcore run as the other character. The game was a nice blast with surprisingly good voice acting for most characters, a fun story that doesn't take itself too seriously and some absolute incredible environments packed with detail and fun use of the fixed camera angle style of the olden days. It becomes clear through a playthrough and especially when you unlock the developer's room after beating the game it's packed with love from the developers.

While I did have a great time, I had some nitpicks. At first on standard difficulty the game presents a fair challenge that will take even survival horror veterans' a bit of time to adapt to. The difficulty however felt a bit too easy after a while imo. Some enemies can be challenging but bosses tend to have the durability of tissue paper. As long as you don't miss shots and go for melee hits when bosses' are left open, you can beat most of them with a small handful of bullets and only a few hits taken. Bosses normally tend to be a resource soak in these games, so this tends to leave you with a lot of health and ammo afterwards. The game has a hardcore difficulty but an in-between hard mode might be a good compromise.

The auto-aim could also be more lenient and forgiving. While the 180 snap-lock of the older RE games was probably a bit too much, here I often have to tap switch target after doing a quick turn to try and make sure I've locked onto an enemy. Sometimes if you shoot too quickly after turning your shot might not register which can be annoying. I also wish the game was a little longer, but the pacing is quite tight and it's likely the developers didn't want to risk overextending the game (I just wish the school section was longer!)

Despite my critiques the game's a blast. If you like older survival horror titles or horror in general (especially cheesy 80 horror), you'll have a great time with this. I really hope this does well and we see more from this developer!

An earnest attempt at a homage to the survival horror classics but not without its flaws. I do particularly like the game's grindhouse aesthetic (think House of the Dead: Overkill).

One thing the first three Silent Hill games understood was that having long open stretches in the town sections required a moving dynamic camera at pretty much all times. Attempting to do these with a mostly fixed shot forces the camera to have to zoom out very far, making your character small at times. Making the town to a realistic scale also means long boring stretches of running in a single direction (an issue I've had with the original Silent Hill games). There are also instances where your character may appear in a noticeably different spot on the screen when changing angles which can be disorienting (although tank controls at least preserve your momentum). This can also lead to trouble identifying your character among a large horde of enemies you're trying to kite around. The dedicated 180 turn button is good although I would have liked the option to also press back and run to perform the same action. For the indoor sections, the fixed camera setting works fine.

The game's puzzles are all fine. None of them have confusing or obtuse solutions though you may have trouble understanding some clues if English isn't your first language as a lot of them are simply poems written on walls. It's generally pretty clear where you have to use a certain key item by the time you find it.

Combat is mostly fine as well. I would have liked a stronger auto aim to deal with the more nimble enemies and bosses but it works well enough. The lack of a reload button and having to use the menu or emptying your weapon feels odd. The game forces a reload animation after you use the menu but that's only for the weapon you're currently equipped with. You can get around this limitation but simply reloading a gun you don't have equipped to avoid the reload animation which is funny. Though you can't switch weapons if you're already doing the loading animation for your current one. There is also a disparity between the amount of gunpowder in the game and the kits needed to turn them into ammo. Inventory space is limited but I personally prefer this to Silent Hill's infinite size and lack of item boxes. There is also a dodge mechanic although you only seem to be able to dodge forward which is weird. Ground Zero does this better by allowing you to dodge in all directions.

A few minor tweaks here and there would help the game a fair amount.

1. Let me listen to audio logs while walking around the room I'm currently in instead of forcing me to stay in the journal screen.

2. Do not make the wax items for saving auto stack whenever I put them in the item box. This way they get used up every 2-3 saves and I don't have to waste 30 seconds throwing them back into the box every time I die and reload my save. I could carry them on me at all times to alleviate this problem except then it's a wasted spot in my inventory and half the dead bodies you search in this game give you more of them without warning which also makes the item stack.

3. Let me 180 turn by pressing back and run.

4. The final boss has an issue where he can pin you against an object and his collision prevents you from running around him even when he's stunned. This happened when I was in areas picking up items the developer had deliberately left in the boss room.

Though I have to say the prices for the DLC outfits are a bit egregious (judging from the game's Kickstarter, the extra outfits should have just been included with the base game since the funding goal for them was met).

Flesh Made Fear is a retro styled survival horror game complete with fixed cameras and tank controls. The game has you explore the outskirts of a town, sewers, and inside various buildings throughout. There are 2 characters you can play as, each with a different game route. I would say each character explores about 85% of the same area, with 15% being original with different bosses to fight. The game took me approximately 5 hours to complete my first playthrough with one character. It took me exactly 15 hours to 100% the whole game and all of its achievements.

*HIGHLY recommend using a controller for this game. There are a few quick time events that are a breeze when using a controller. Also due to the tank controls, a controller really helps dodging zombies with ease.
The controls are second nature if you grew up playing RE(1-3) on Playstation.

+ From the opening menu screen, the synthwave music just smashes throughout and sounds amazing. 
+ The atmosphere is gorgeous, creepy, with many interesting buildings and places to explore. The neon aesthetic is beautiful.
+ The voice acting is well done in a cheesy way. Also most of the collectible notes are read through by voice actors, a nice touch of immersion.
+ There is a secret infinite weapon to unlock if you find all the plushies hidden in the game and beat the game on hardcore mode. This weapon is hilarious and lots of fun to use while mopping up post game achievements.
+ The story at first sounds simple and cliche, but there are many notes to discover for those who want to deep dive into it if they so choose. This leaves it up to the player to choose how much they want to learn the backstory, which is perfect.
+ The puzzles are well balanced, not too difficult or obscure, no guide needed.
+ Several bosses are disgustingly hilarious, and well designed.
+ Excellent replay value. Perfect game for speed runs.
+ The levels / layout of the game is large and well made.

- There are a few instances where you are ambushed by hoards of 10+ zombies that you need to dodge / run around. Fortunately there are save stations everywhere to help you. Also use your knives and dodge button, they are immensely useful. 
- A few areas are a bit too dark. I would have lightened up a few areas about 10% brightness.
- There are a bit too many achievements for all the endings, there are about 6. I would have switched this around to add more achievements for collecting notes, and adding a New Game+ mode. 

This game is one of the best, if not THE best, homages out there to the original Resident Evil games.
Lets get a sequel!

Overall: 9.5/10

They've somehow managed to balance the silly humour of over the top horror with some very dark lore in a way that doesn't feel like either part doesn't belong.

The game runs fairly well on Steam Deck as well. I have the LCD Steam Deck and managed to play through this at a solid 60 on Low Settings.

Only encountered a few very minor bugs whilst playing and most of what you could want gameplay settings wise is there. For me it's only missing a few small things like toggle run.

Excited to see what comes next from this team.

Embrace the Jank and enjoy a really great game and soundtrack.

I received a copy from the developer as I did some voice direction and audio mastering for the game. I'm really glad I managed to stay mostly spoiler-free until the release because this is, by far, one of the best horror games, and *the* best indie horror game i have had the pleasure of playing.

The voice acting was incredible, especially by RJ Green, who portrayed The Ripper, Bill, the prologue voice, and one other fun cameo. He is one of the most talented voice actors I've come across and I can't wait to see where his talents take him.

But the entire cast should be incredibly proud of their work. The end result is nothing short of fantastic. The story is told through both character interaction and found cassette tapes, and everything is brilliantly written. And the actors bring that story to life with impassioned, vibrant performances.

As for the game itself, the art style is a beautiful homage to retro survival horror, with some truly memorable visuals. Gruesome in the very best way. The music is stunning, the sound design impeccably sets the mood and works seamlessly with the brilliantly placed fixed camera angles to build tension and create a setting that keeps players nerves on edge.

The tank controls, limited resources, and constant tension deliver the perfect survival horror experience. The enemies and bosses are incredibly designed - both artistically and technically, difficult in their way but not so overpowered that the player begins to feel helpless, and every one you defeat feels like a true accomplishment. 

This game is absolutely worth your time. I anticipate many, many playthroughs in my future.

Thank you for creating such a masterpiece. It was well worth the wait.

Great homage to classic games like Silent Hill and Resident Evil. And the creator of this game did a good job of capturing the essence of 90s horror and turning it up a notch. If this is what Tainted Pact can come up with, i'm looking forward to his future creative projects and what he can come up with. This is a piece of art. The puzzles are very simple and not over-done at all. I'm playing a horror game, not solving a lab experiment. Level gameplay is very straight-forward and you don't get lost. And it has had great support from a streamer community which do the voice acting. Thumbs up since all this was put together by one dude so show some love to indie games <3

Good horror game, I enjoyed it but some of mid-game the bosses are a bit unfair. Other than that, solid, 8.5/100

ALSO THE SHOTGUN SLAPS

If you like Classic Survival Horror games like Resident Evil or Silent Hill... then this game should definetly be in your Library!
And the soundtrack is an absolute BANGER!!

Wow this game blew way past my expectations! This has been a great year for survival horror, but it seemed like Silent Hill has largely been the raison d’etre for indie devs in 2025. But like a bat out of hell, Flesh Made Fear delivers a true classic Resident Evil style game, and does so with so much grace.

It is soaking wet in 80’s slasher horror film kitsch, and makes no apologies for it. The soundtrack is incredible, with pulsing synths that John Carpenter would absolutely approve of. The voice acting is pretty much a perfect replica of the classic Resident Evil style, with its over the top caricatures-as-characters (the main antagonist being the most over the top example). The enemies are completely absurd body horror creations by Ripper, the mad scientist who has turned the town of Rotwood into an amusement park of horror.

Everything is just… perfect. Perfect goofy tone, perfect puzzles, satisfying combat, fun exploration. If I could think of one tiny complaint - the map is borderline useless. It is very zoomed out and only gives a broad city-wide overview, so no tracking locked doors or puzzles. But to be honest, the level design didn’t really need it, so I won’t knock off any points there. 

This is definitely in my top 3 for the year so far, alongside Heartworm and Tormented Souls 2. If you enjoyed Nightmare of Decay, The Lacerator, Classic Resident Evil, or even just cult classic horror films
like Evil Dead - this is the easiest recommendation in the world. I had a blast from the beginning to the end, and I can’t wait to jump back in for the second character campaign.

9.8/10, amazing work.
Well made classic fixed camera survival horror. That's all you need.

Great game! As a lover of OG Resident Evil this was a blast to play through. True classic survival horror, tank controls, fixed camera angles, small puzzles, the devs knew what they wanted to do with the game. Reminded me of playing RE1 & RE2 og again. Hope to see Flesh Made Fear 2 where an even bigger map will be made.

Also, it is worth to collect all plushies and finish the game on hardcore. Pass the gas!

Pretty great game for people who enjoy PSX horror games like the OG Resident Evil trilogy and Silent Hill games. Not the hardest game out there but that's fine. Just wish the game gave you more ammo for the grenade launcher (or if there is ammo to be picked up for the grenade launcher I never found it outside of the Gunpowder Type Ds you find in the same room as the grenade launcher) and that's about it. Maybe a harder difficulty that makes the enemies and bosses deal more damage and are a bit more tanky would also be nice but other than that other than that I give this game a solid 9/10.

It's a resident evil clone but a very very good one.

The game is cheap, compact and very good.

The bosses and their designs were badass, and the different weapons spiced up the gameplay. While I wish I the story was a bit longer, I hope to play more games by this dev team in the future. :)

Bloody good game, music was very atmospheric, at points it seems stupid hard or tricky till you work it out i definitely be replaying this game

What can i say, great nostalgic survival horror with good old B-movie voice acting. I took my time during play through and enjoyed every minute of it, i hope the developer goes down this route again in the future. (R.I.P - Rufus)

Flesh Made Fear takes obvious inspiration from the old-school Resident Evil and Alone in the Dark with the fixed camera angles, somewhat infamous "tank controls" which I love, cheesy but still entertaining voice acting but the most important things: The story building up to the excuse so you can encounter zombies and other mutated monsters.
The violence is over the top, reminding me of the b-horror movies from the 80s with over-the-top gore.
Highly recommended for any horror fan!

Flesh Made Fear is truly a love letter to the original PSX Resident Evil games. I enjoyed the gory environments and the campy cast of characters. The boss fights were frustratingly tough in a fun way. The corny voice acting was very endearing. It felt like a cheesy 90's horror movie and made me laugh many times!

Backer for the game but this doesnt reflect my opinion of the game.

The game is awesome and well worth your time if you love PS1 style retro horror games like classic Resident Evil, Silent Hill and Alone in the Dark.

While I do have a few gripes with it, I overall had a very enjoyable time with this.

This game snuck up on me, but I'm really happy to have discovered and played it. There are a ton of indie survival horror titles coming out these days but Flesh Made Fear is worth your attention.

The strongest thing Flesh Made Fear has going for it is its presentation. It feels like a playable grindhouse film and a lot of care was put into the story, the characters, and most importantly the storytelling. Every character and cut scene is fully voiced. Instead of journal entries, you get fully voiced recordings. The R.I.P. squad are all likable and I immediately found myself hoping to spend more time with them in another game. For anyone who gets this reference, they feel a bit like the BPRD to me.

Graphics wise, the game looks like an old PS1 title and it's appropriately creepy and moody throughout. There's also some great environmental storytelling and very pleasant sprite based menu elements that are very charming to look at.

This is definitely a survival horror title, but I feel like Tainted Pact really wants you to experience the whole story, so you get plenty of tools and resources to make it to the end and the game isn't too long. Your knives (that's right, you have two of them) can eviscerate any solo zombie, and there's plenty of healing and ammo items available in the normal difficulty. There are also tons of save rooms and item boxes. That said, you can die VERY QUICKLY if you get swarmed so you should save often and enjoy the ride. There are also a handful of puzzles and some item fetching. None of the puzzles ever really challenge you all that much, but they do break up the pacing a bit.

I'm hoping we haven't seen the last of the R.I.P. squad.

I'm not big on horror games but i have tried some over the years. This is the first game i can say i have beaten with both main characters. Right from the start i could see the inspiration from games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill. The PSX retro style and the controls are "Chef's Kiss". I felt like a teenager playing the OG Resident Evil again. The story and the atmosphere really shined here. The game never felt like a slog or overly complicated. The puzzles and the cryptic messages were decent enough to figure out. When i finished playing the first playthrough i instantly started up my 2nd playthrough. I also enjoyed the fact that both characters have thier own locations to explore and bosses to fight. I wish i could forget this game just so i could play it again fresh with all the jump scares and twists again. I will try to start my 3rd playthrough on hardcore mode just to get all the extra Easter eggs and such.
Very good game. Can tell lots of passion went into this one.

Only gripe is the achievements require multiple endings, there's quite a few too. You can make saves as the ending 'choices' are near to the end but it's still a pain and could have been done better honestly.

Would recommend this game 100% though, for the price what you're getting is a great SH game.

Definitely recommend this game. Its atmosphere, puzzles, presentation, enemy variety, style and most importantly combat is very well done. I only wish it has more things to do because I still want to play it again. 
Fixed camera tilt effect is a little bit overused but it did not bother me. I enjoyed every bit. I still recommend it if you are first to this genre, because it is also forgiving. If you are already played classic resident evil games, you still will not be disappointed either.

What a fantastic game! Love the return of fixed camera angles and tank controls.

This is the type of grindhouse, B-horror movie jank that I'm here for. 
Flesh made Fear wears it's Resident Evil roots on its sleeve and isn't coy about that fact.

It's memey, it has jokes, it doesn't take itself seriously - and it's a hell of a fun homage as a result.
Truly a love letter to the indie horror-playing community with cameo performances and collectables from various streamers, a playthrough of FmF doesn't overstay its welcome and will take roughly 5-7 hours per character - of which there are two. 

It features all the classic survival horror hallmarks such as fixed camera angles, limited resources, tank controls, multiple endings, puzzle solving, inventory management, all driven by the pursuit of a cheesy villain who absolutely chews the scenery in all his performances!

An ambitious success for Tainted Pact. 
Recommended if you want to laugh and relive some of the the corny RE 1 days.

This is easily one of the best PSX survival horror throwback, I've ever played. Not only featuring two playable character with their own scenario, but it also has multiple endings as well. There are many Resident Evil clones (or RESY games as I like to call it) out there similar to this. But this game stands of it all.

My only complaint that I have for the game is most of the content has been left out, less weapons and monsters, and the typing sounds with the text.

This is Tainted Pact Games latest and best release, and I praise them for that. I can only say one thing for this game... "SEQUEL PLEASE" 🙏 🙏 🙏 

I think I want to go back and play the old Resident Evil Trilogy after this.

This was a fun little game I got for backing the kickstarter.  It's like a miniature Resident Evil but more campy.  I've played through both characters stories and there is some differences per playthrough, the most notable being some new areas and a boss that's exclusive to each character.  The girl has less health but makes up for it with more inventory while the guy is the opposite.  I personally found the girl's campaign easier then the guys as the increased inventory was far more valuable for me.  Like Resident Evil and even Dino Crisis there is a system where you can combine items to make more ammo.  Your knifes are a great weapon, but only in one on one cases, I did manage to beat a boss here or there with the knifes as well once I was out of ammo.  From my experience in this game, it's better to avoid combat if possible so to have ammo for the bosses but this game will throw you into situations where you need to fight. especially in some areas where you are facing a horde of enemies.  I've managed to find all but one collectable but I can't seem to figure out where the last is after multiple plays.  For me the best part of this game was the main villain himself, The Ripper, he reminds me of Freddy Krueger with his humor and some of the audio logs.  I hope to see a sequel or DLC in the future as I had a great time with this game.  The only two issues I had were the Joystick controls don't work well with the camera angles, so stick to the D-pad for movement.  Sometimes you will get cornered by the horde and that's it game over.  But it two cases I got corned by the boss and couldn't get around him no matter what and died because I ran out of ammo and healing while stuck in a corner.  In a sewer section one enemy actually glitched out and I had to restart as I couldn't hit him or get around him as was stuck while his friends couldn't reach me either do to him blocking them as well. Hardcore mode was fun as well, if you want a bit more of a challenge, I wouldn't recommend it as a first playthrough though, do it after you've learned the routes/enemies/item locations otherwise it might be a bit much for some people.

Tainted Pact delivers once again. Safe to say Michael has a pretty good pulse on the horror genre, each game trying new ideas, styles, and more ambitious than the previous title.

Flesh Made Fear is a tribute to the PS1 era horror titles; in particular Resident Evil in this case. 

+Amazing ambience and OST is really good.
+Gun-play is pretty solid.
+Visual aesthetic is fantastic, from the pixel graphics style, to the gore, and character models are exactly what you'd expect for a game of this caliber.
+Hardcore difficulty is definitely tuned tighter than normal mode. Health pickups are extremely scarce, and using careful planning and estimation of your resources if vital for survival.
+Voice acting is pretty good! Leans into that old school horror B movie dialogue.
+Inventory management 
+Collectibles to find.

-Some minor gripes. Sometimes weapon shots would clip through a boss if they get right in your face, wasting the ammo and doing no damage. Also I assume it could be a visual bug, but sometimes bandages don't move the HP bar at all, but this could be intentional. 

Overall. If you're looking for a stellar retro style survival horror game. This one should fit the bill. Looking forward to the next one @TaintedPact.

Pros:

+ Presentation is really nice, the chunky, blocky PS1 look of the game is recreated really well, characters and  maps really feel like a 1996 survival horror homage

+ Music is fine, a non intrusive, reasonable creepy set of tunes

+ Combat is snappy and responsive (for old school tank controls) and the dodge is quite a good addition

+ The plot is pure C-Movie cheese that is far too stupid to not love

Cons:

- Exploration is mediocre, apart from plushie collectibles ammo are generally concentrated in very few of the maps leaving entire well designed rooms completely empty of any meaningful reason to explore them

- Puzzles are piss easy, really these are really something a kindergarden child could solve

- The game completely lacks the 'balance' of enemies to create a scary atmosphere, the gore covered rooms are the norm so you get used to them really quickly and putting 15 to 25 enemies in corridors is a very good way to bore the player when its done over and over and over and over

- Voice acting is atrocious...if the intent was to mimic the legendary bad voice acting of RE1 you guys overdid it, its painful to listen to these character yap, thankfully there is a skip button

- Extremely short, you can beat it in around 4 to 5 hours

Flesh made fear is a somewhat competent tribute to old school survival horror that alas does not shine in anyway shape or form compared to todays competition or even recent past (Tormented Souls comes to mind) that being said it is cheap and it is pleasurable for one playtrough.

Super Average but recommended 6/10

This game feels like a low-effort attempt at being Resident Evil — but without the polish, charm, or functionality that makes those games great.It tries so hard to be another survival horror clone, but it just doesn’t land. I have seen other people play it and well the gunplay alone is frustrating enough to turn anyone off. The performance is poor, and the resolution is unreasonably bad when I opened the game for the first time. I couldn't even get the game to stay on one screen.

What also left a bad impression was when looking in the reviews, seeing players who leave honest, constructive negative reviews get mocked or hit with “jester” emojis by the devs or community. Criticism isn’t an insult- it’s feedback. When that’s dismissed or ridiculed, it sends a clear message that the game’s creators aren’t open to improvement. Therefore can't be taken seriously. Take it from Gun Interactive and Papergames (also known as Infold Games).

This game really needs some real work- the mechanics to optimization and community interaction. 
I’m refunding my purchase because of how badly the game runs and is poorly optimized and just overal the game is lacking.

no re-bindable keys, there's qte's, no deadzones for controller, no manual reload and "auto reload" that doesn't work. most of my time in the game was afk. i've played about 10 minutes and I'm already irritated.

I tend to be hard to impress. Unfortunately, I find this game to be just Resident Evil but voiced by streamers. That might seem like an odd thing to say but I literally mean it, it's Resident Evil, with all of the flaws included. It doesn't do anything to separate itself or make itself improved over the original. It's also probably less polished than the original as well, which ends up hurting the overall package. Almost all of the threats in the sections I played can be solved by just shooting and I never seemed to be too low on ammo.

I ended up stopping around when you get the shotgun as they script a 20 zombie ambush right after you pick it up. I killed half of the zombies and left the other half, as to not waste all of the shotgun ammo I had. When I entered one of the motel rooms, I had not realized that the original spawn point for the other half was directly in front of the motel room, which had me quite literally exit the room into a crowd of 10 zombies at point blank because that's where the ambush had originally placed them.

If you really like Resident Evil 1, with every flaw (and more) included and voiced by streamers, go for it. If not, I'd say you're better off without it.

This game... Could use some work. It's fairly new, so I'm hoping the devs might fix some of these issues in a later update, but I'll say, I'm struggling to not just give up on it.

First, I couldn't for the life of me get this game to play in a 16:10 aspect ratio (the OLED Steam Deck's native resolution) without it cutting out a bit of the far right and left of the screen.

Second, this game's controller support as it is makes the analog stick deadzone way too small which made both my Steam Deck and DualSense appear if they had stick drift while aiming, which really wasn't difficult to fix on Steam Deck, but I fear it could lead to some negative reviews in the future to customers who'd be nonethewiser.

Third, enemies have the ability to pin you against the wall and make running to the left or right of them impossible leaving you to either waste ammo or die, which isn't ideal for a game in a genre that prioritizes fight or flight.

The story itself, though? I'm only at the police station so far, but I'm genuinely enthralled with the narrative, so I imagine it'd be worth it for anyone willing to play right now.

I'll change this review if any of this changes.

Give me jester rewards if you work as a cleanup crew floor licker for messy bukkake sessions.

I wish it wasn't the case but I can't recommend this game. With all the indie horror games I play, this one just let me down the most by being so aggressive out of the gate even on normal difficulty. I played just like I do a standard RE game trying to kite and skirt by with just the bare minimum - then they give you the shotgun and surround you with 15+ zombies - they are easy to skirt but this game seems to work on RE3 style mob placements where you need to go 2-3 screens to reset aggro. So you can't just rush objectives without wasting time to save ammo - you're stuck wasting time running through random fucking pathways trying to reset aggro so you can dodge spam to the next area so you can proceed to ammo dump into an extremely beefcake boss that gets old in the first 2 minutes of bland attack patterns. 

It's a great game on paper that would have been fantastic if bosses weren't just bullet sponges, and/or aggro reset on a single door. 

So yeah, I took the chance hoping that this would be another Tainted Pact special - a weird buggy mess that barely worked but had so much charm that it was fun to experience like Suffer the Night, Terror at Oakheart, or Massacre at the Mirage - but instead I just got a weird aftertaste in my mouth of playing some janky "trying to be serious" RE clone without any of the charm of either - early RE or pre-TP releases.
